pr.title: Consider errors in MIR as impossible predicates to empty the body.
pr.description:
The ICEs come from elaborating drops or performing state transform in MIR bodies that fail typeck or borrowck.

If the body is tainted, replace it with `unreachable`.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/122630
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/122904
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/125185
Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/139556

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.summary: ImpossiblePredicates must treat a MIR body tainted by earlier typeck/borrowck errors as "impossible" and replace its body with a single `unreachable`, not only bodies whose elaborated predicates reference errors or are impossible. The PR fixes ICEs caused by later drop elaboration / state transform running over bodies that failed typeck or borrowck, including recursive TAIT/drop-elaboration and coroutine move cases, and changes expected diagnostics for const promotion.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, `ImpossiblePredicates::run_pass` only inspected the item's predicates: it instantiated `tcx.predicates_of(body.source.def_id())`, filtered out clauses with `HAS_FREE_LOCAL_NAMES` or `HAS_CT_PROJECTION`, elaborated them with `traits::elaborate`, then cleared the body only when `predicates.references_error() || traits::impossible_predicates(tcx, predicates)` held. Exact old code from the diff: `if predicates.references_error() || traits::impossible_predicates(tcx, predicates) {`. It did not consult `body.tainted_by_errors`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior was leaving a tainted MIR body unchanged: when typeck/borrowck had already recorded errors in the body, but the item's elaborated predicates did not themselves reference errors and were not impossible, the pass skipped the clearing transformation. Downstream MIR processing then attempted drop elaboration or state transform on a body that failed typeck/borrowck, producing ICEs. The PR's fixed transformation adds `body.tainted_by_errors.is_some()` to the condition: `let impossible = body.tainted_by_errors.is_some() || has_impossible_predicates(tcx, body.source.def_id());`. When true, the pass performs the existing clearing: `// Clear the body to only contain a single `unreachable` statement.` The predicate logic itself is only refactored into `has_impossible_predicates`; the new semantic input is body taint.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies generated for functions/constants/closures whose type checking or borrow checking has already failed, especially: bodies involving `type_alias_impl_trait` opaque aliases and recursive calls that feed drop elaboration; coroutines with moves across yields; and const/promoted expressions with borrow errors. Valid comparison programs should be identical except that one leaves the body tainted by a typeck/borrowck error while the other repairs the error, so the predicate-only check would be equal but the taint input differs.
analysis.trigger: Run the ImpossiblePredicates MIR pass on a body for which `body.tainted_by_errors.is_some()` is true even though `predicates.references_error() || traits::impossible_predicates(tcx, predicates)` is false. In that situation the pre-fix pass left the failing body intact, and later MIR phases such as drop elaboration or state transform could ICE instead of producing ordinary diagnostics.
preconditions: The function/const body failed typeck or borrowck and therefore has `tainted_by_errors` set.
The item's elaborated predicates do not by themselves reference errors and are not impossible, so the old predicate-only condition is false.
A later MIR phase (drop elaboration or state transform) runs on the body before compilation aborts.
Regression shapes include TAIT `#[define_opaque]` opaque types with closures moving out of shared references, and coroutine move-across-yield bodies.
pitfalls: Do not equate `predicates.references_error()` with body taint: errors may exist only in the MIR body after typeck/borrowck, while the item's predicates look clean.
The pass is not a general error suppressor; it must still clear the body to a single `unreachable`, matching the existing comment `// Clear the body to only contain a single `unreachable` statement.`
The refactor extracting `has_impossible_predicates` does not itself change predicate semantics; the behavioral fix is adding the `body.tainted_by_errors.is_some()` disjunct.

Changing which bodies get emptied also changes expected diagnostics: `tests/ui/consts/promoted_const_call2` loses the `E0493` destructor-at-compile-time error and drops from 5 to 4 errors after the fix.
Deleted `tests/crashes/*` known-bug files are not evidence that a replacement pass is wrong; they are converted into regression tests under `tests/ui`.
analysis.testStrategy: Use UI regression tests with `-Zvalidate-mir` for tainted-body cases and verify ordinary diagnostics rather than ICEs. Convert known-bug crash tests into UI tests as the PR does: `tests/ui/coroutine/moved-twice.rs` (regression for #122630), `tests/ui/type-alias-impl-trait/recursive-drop-elaboration.rs` (#122904), `tests/ui/type-alias-impl-trait/recursive-drop-elaboration-2.rs` (#139556), and `tests/ui/type-alias-impl-trait/type-error-drop-elaboration.rs` (#125185) all use bodies that fail type/borrow checking. Include a paired program with the same structure but without the failing move/type error to show the body is only emptied when tainted. For const promotion, update `tests/ui/consts/promoted_const_call2` expectations because the tainted const body is now unreachable and the `E0493` drop-elaboration error disappears. Do not claim execution; inspect the supplied .stderr expectations.

If the body is tainted, replace it with `unreachable`.
